name: Nancy Quan
current_role: EVP and Global Chief Technical & Innovation Officer, The Coca-Cola Company
profile: Purdue-trained food/nutrition scientist who spent years at Mars Inc. (R&D, business development, manufacturing) before joining Coca-Cola in 2007 as R&D GM for Europe/Eurasia in Brussels. Rose through Global R&D Officer and CTO roles; now EVP overseeing technical, innovation and supply chain for all Coca-Cola brands, reporting to CEO James Quincey.
interesting_fact: She led a redesign of Coca-Cola's plastic bottles in India that cut plastic use by 38% without sacrificing quality or carbonation.
deep_cut_fact: Grew up in Newton County, Indiana, was starting point guard and valedictorian at South Newton High; her first job out of Purdue (after a Mars internship) was on the Dove chocolate line, where she helped develop heat-stable chocolate for troops in the Middle East. Received Purdue HHS Distinguished Alumni Award (2025).
notes: Corporate executive (wealth from KO equity). Reach via Coca-Cola media relations. Reportedly also a non-exec director of Coca-Cola Europacific Partners (secondary source, unverified).

name: Alfred Lee Finley
current_role: Director, GBank Financial Holdings (Las Vegas); President/owner of BFX Fire (wildland fire trucks), Fort Worth
profile: Vancouver-born entrepreneur (UBC economics) who has worked in the utility-equipment business since 1969 and founded BFX Fire, a maker of wildland fire trucks, and heads Air Shelters USA. Holds real estate across 10 states, has lived in Fort Worth since 1990, and has been a director and 10%+ owner of Nevada-based GBank since 2013; joined Medalist Diversified REIT's board in 2024.
interesting_fact: Besides banking, he founded and owns BFX Fire, a manufacturer of wildland fire trucks, and heads Air Shelters USA; he also holds real estate across 10 states.
deep_cut_fact: He began his career in the utility equipment business in Vancouver, B.C. back in 1969, decades before moving to Fort Worth in 1990.
notes: Private, low-profile businessman; no personal published contacts found. Was a 2026 GBank Class 1 director nominee (MarketBeat). Aggregators show Medalist board role ended early 2026 (unverified). Best route likely via GBank investor relations or BFX Fire Apparatus company channels. BFX Fire Apparatus (Weatherford, TX factory) supplies wildland engines to agencies such as the BLM and Texas A&M Forest Service (per firehouse.com / TFS purchase orders).

name: Vivek Shah
current_role: Chief Executive Officer, Ziff Davis, Inc. (Nasdaq: ZD)
profile: Tufts political-science grad who joined Time Warner/Time Inc. in 1995, rising to president of the Fortune/Money Group and group president, digital. In 2010 he bought tech publisher Ziff Davis with Great Hill Partners; after J2 Global acquired it in 2012 he became J2's CEO (2018) and led its rebrand as Ziff Davis (2021), a portfolio including IGN, Mashable, PCMag, Speedtest/Ookla and CNET (acquired 2024).
interesting_fact: He personally led the 2010 buyout of Ziff Davis with private equity firm Great Hill Partners, then ended up running the much larger acquirer (J2 Global) and renaming it after the company he bought.
deep_cut_fact: He serves on the board of StreetSquash, a New York youth-enrichment program combining squash with academics, and on the CUNY Craig Newmark Graduate School of Journalism Foundation board; he was also IAB chairman in 2014 and a Crain's NY 40 Under 40 in 2006.
notes: Tufts University trustee. Media/digital publishing CEO — Ziff Davis owns tech outlets (PCMag, CNET, Mashable, Speedtest), relevant to data-center/tech audience.

name: Jason Aryeh
current_role: Founder & Managing General Partner, JALAA Equities LP; director of Ligand Pharmaceuticals, Orchestra BioMed and Lifecore Biomedical
profile: Life-sciences investor who founded JALAA Equities in 1997, a Greenwich, CT-based private fund focused on biotech and medical devices. Independent director of Ligand Pharmaceuticals since 2006 (chairs its nominating & governance committee), and sits on the boards of Orchestra BioMed, Lifecore Biomedical and Anebulo Pharmaceuticals.
interesting_fact: Has served on Ligand Pharmaceuticals' board for roughly two decades (since 2006), through its transformation into a royalty/technology-licensing model (e.g. Captisol).
notes: Low public profile; holds a B.A. in economics (honors) from Colgate. No verified personal/fund contacts found; best route via Ligand investor relations or board correspondence.

name: Max Broden
current_role: Senior EVP & Chief Financial Officer, Aflac Incorporated; director, Trupanion
profile: Swedish-born finance executive (Stockholm School of Economics, CFA) who spent 2007-2017 as a senior portfolio manager at Norges Bank Investment Management analysing global insurers. Joined Aflac in 2017 as SVP & Treasurer, became deputy CFO in 2019, CFO in January 2020 and senior EVP in 2025; also sits on pet-insurer Trupanion's board.
interesting_fact: Before running Aflac's finances he spent a decade on the buy side at Norges Bank (manager of Norway's sovereign wealth fund), doing deep fundamental analysis of global insurance companies.
deep_cut_fact: At Norges Bank he specialised in select global insurance names including strategic investments, then went from investor to insurer, joining Aflac as Treasurer in April 2017 and rising to CFO in under three years.

public_contacts.value: dyoung@aflac.com (David A. Young, Aflac investor & rating agency relations)

notes: Corporate CFO; does quarterly 'CFO video updates' for Aflac results, so is comfortable on camera. Route via Aflac media relations.

name: Thomas W Seger
current_role: Owner/director of Indiana agribusinesses (Wabash Valley Produce, Simple Transport); former lead independent director, German American Bancorp (2011-2024)
profile: Southern Indiana agribusiness owner with 40+ years in poultry and agriculture: holds ownership interests in Wabash Valley Produce (large poultry producer, Dubois, IN, where he was formerly president), Simple Transport and Farbest Foods (Huntingburg, IN). Served on German American Bancorp's board from 2011 as lead independent director, resigning effective Dec 31, 2024 ahead of the Heartland BancCorp merger.
interesting_fact: His wealth comes largely from a big stake (~680k shares) in Jasper, Indiana-based German American Bancorp, whose bank was founded in 1910 by local German-American business leaders.
deep_cut_fact: Chaired German American Bancorp's Governance/Nominating Committee and was valued by the board for his perspective on the agricultural industry 'on a local, regional, and national level' from over 40 years in poultry.
notes: Very private rural-Indiana businessman; no published personal or office contacts found. Alive status not independently confirmed after 2024 (no obituary found in brief search). Not an obvious energy/data-center guest.

name: F Scott Dueser
current_role: Executive Chairman, First Financial Bankshares, Inc. (Abilene, TX)
profile: Abilene banker (Texas Tech '75, Southwestern Graduate School of Banking '81) who ran First Financial Bank Abilene 1991-2001, became President & CEO of holding company First Financial Bankshares in 2001 and chairman in 2008, building it into one of Texas's largest and most valuable regional banks. Handed the CEO role to David Bailey in January 2026 and remains Executive Chairman.
interesting_fact: He has chaired both the Texas Tech University Board of Regents and the Texas Bankers Association.
deep_cut_fact: Named the Abilene Chamber of Commerce's Outstanding Citizen of the Year in 2009; has also chaired United Way of Abilene, the Cisco College Advisory Board and Abilene's Day Nursery.
notes: Releases list CFO Michelle Hickox (phone, Abilene HQ) as contact; no published press email found. Prominent West Texas civic figure; Texas Tech connection may be a good hook.

name: Ben M Palmer
current_role: President & CEO, RPC, Inc. (oilfield services, Atlanta) — retiring by end of 2026; former CEO of Marine Products Corp (acquired by MasterCraft, May 2026)
profile: Longtime finance chief of the Rollins-family companies: CFO of RPC (oil & gas services) from 1996 and of Marine Products (Chaparral/Robalo boats) from its 2001 spin-off. Became CEO of both in 2022; led Marine Products into its ~$232M sale to MasterCraft (closed May 2026). RPC announced in June 2026 he will retire by year-end 2026.
interesting_fact: He simultaneously ran an oilfield-services company (RPC, pressure pumping/frac services) and a boat builder (Chaparral and Robalo) — both legacy Rollins family businesses.
deep_cut_fact: Before joining RPC in 1996 he spent three years as CFO of EQ Services, a commercial mortgage and asset-management subsidiary of The Equitable Companies.
notes: Energy-sector angle (oilfield services) fits the podcast. Retiring end of 2026 — may have more availability in 2027.
